stories.title: Israel warns of 'forceful' response to kites flown from Gaza
stories.summary: Israel has warned Hamas that it will increase strikes on Gaza following concern over launches of kites, drones and balloons from the territory. Several kites - which were not carrying explosives - were found in an Israeli community near the border with Gaza over the weekend, local media reported. "Forceful actions will be taken to put an end to this phenomenon," Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz said on Monday. Before the war, kites and balloons carrying incendiary devices were launched into Israel, causing fires that burned forest and farmland. Hamas has denied responsibility for the new kites and said they belonged to "children searching for their innocent childhood amid the rubble". The group also accused Israel of using the kites as a "pretext" for continued air strikes in Gaza despite the ceasefire agreed last October. Four kites were found in Kibbutz Nahal Oz, which is about 800m (2,620ft) from the Gaza border, on Friday and Saturday. Several more were found elsewhere in southern Israel last week, according to local media. The Israeli reports cited military sources as saying they believed Hamas was behind the kites and that they might have been intended to test Israel's response. No suspicious materials were attached to the kites and that they did not pose a threat, the military said. But Katz warned there would be "zero tolerance" and said "a balloon is treated like a kite, and a kite is treated like a drone, with or without explosives." Residents of Nahal Oz said in a statement that they feared the return of incendiary kites and balloons, adding: "We will not accept a policy of containment when it comes to our security."

stories.title: Russia prioritizes oil, gas projects with India, hydrocarbon supplies — Manturov
stories.summary: Russia also sees potential for new joint projects with India in the extraction and processing of nonferrous, rare and rare-earth metals, the Russian First Deputy PM stated
article_sentences: "We attach priority importance to cooperation in the field of energy security.
This concerns not only supplies of oil, petroleum products, and coal, but also joint investment projects in hydrocarbon production and processing," he noted.
Earlier, Russian Energy Minister Sergey Tsivilyov said that India remained a key partner for Russia’s fuel and energy sector and that oil supplies remained at a high level.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak also noted that Russia was interested in attracting Indian investment in its oil and gas sector, as well as developing a distribution network in India with the participation of Russian companies.
Russia also sees potential for new joint projects with India in the extraction and processing of nonferrous, rare, and rare-earth metals, Manturov said.
"We see potential for expanding cooperation in metallurgy and mining, including the joint development of deposits and the processing of nonferrous, rare, and rare-earth metals," he noted.
India will serve as the partner country of the international Russian Energy Week (REW) forum this year, becoming the first official partner country in the event’s history.

stories.title: Russian expert points at lack of substantive agenda for Witkoff, Kushner’s visit
stories.summary: According to Ivan Timofeyev, the fact that Russian-US consultations and opinion exchanges are ongoing is a good thing, but they don't seem to yield any practical results
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 24.

A visit to Russia by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner is being postponed due to a lack of substantive agenda, Director General of the Russian International Affairs Council Ivan Timofeyev told TASS in an interview.
He recalled Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s remarks that President Vladimir Putin was ready to once again meet with Witkoff and Kushner, but "it’s a question of what they will bring."
"Any consultations and negotiations are based on a specific agenda and require at least a theoretical prospect of reaching a solution, some kind of an algorithm."
"Along with negotiations, any settlement process involves de-escalation measures.
But this is quite the opposite of what we are seeing now, as Ukraine has intensified its strikes and Russia has responded," the expert continued.
"Western media portrayed these strikes as some sort of a game changer, which is supposed to force Russia to make concessions.
As you can see, this did not happen.
I don’t think that this kind of escalation will contribute to any sort of settlement."
"The fact that Russian-US consultations and opinion exchanges are ongoing is a good thing, but, so far, I don’t see them yielding any practical results," Timofeyev added.
A source earlier told TASS that the visit to Russia by Witkoff and Kushner is being delayed, and "there are reasons to postpone it.".
